title: Slider
lead: A Slider represents an input that allows user to choose a value from within a specific range.

examples.name: Size
examples.description: A slider comes in both medium and small size. Medium is the default.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.description:
A slider can be a controlled input where the slider value is stored in state
      and updated with `onChange`. This is also useful for setting custom aria-valuetext

examples.name: Step
examples.description: You can define the step value of a slider so that the value will always be a mutiple of that step

examples.name: Min Max
examples.description: A slider with min and max values displayed

examples.name: Vertical
examples.description: A slider can be oriented vertically where the max value is at the top of the slider.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.description: A disabled slider will not change or fire events on click or keyboard press.

prose.text:
## Best practices

### Layout

- Don't use a slider for binary settings.
- Don't use a continuous slider if the range of values is large.
- Don't use for a range with fewer than three values.
- Sliders are typically horizontal but can be vertical, when needed.

### Content

- Use step points if you don't want the slider to allow arbitrary values between minimum and maximum.

rows: The root of the Slider. The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified directly on the `<Slider>`. All other native props will be applied to the primary slot, `input`.

The hidden input for the Slider. This is the PRIMARY slot: all native properties specified directly on `<Slider>` will be applied to this slot, except `className` and `style`, which remain on the root slot.
The number of steps that the Slider's `value` will increment upon change. When provided, the Slider will snap to the closest available value. This must be a positive value.
Whether to render the Slider as disabled.
The Slider's base. It is used to visibly display the min and max selectable values.
The draggable icon used to select a given value from the Slider. This is the element containing `role = 'slider'`.
The max value of the Slider.
The min value of the Slider.

Orient is a non standard attribute that allows for vertical orientation in Firefox. It is set internally when `vertical` is set to true. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/range#non_standard_attributes Webkit/Chromium support for vertical inputs is provided via -webkit-appearance css property
The starting value for an uncontrolled Slider. Mutually exclusive with `value` prop.
The current value of the controlled Slider. Mutually exclusive with `defaultValue` prop.
Render the Slider in a vertical orientation, smallest value on the bottom.
Triggers a callback when the value has been changed. This will be called on every individual step.
